newsitem.title: UK: Copper physical premiums hit by backwardation.
newsitem.headline: Copper physical premiums hit by backwardation.

text.p: The current high backwardation on the London Metal Exchange (LME) copper market has washed through the physical sector in Europe, dampening business and affecting premiums, traders said.

The LME is currently passing through a well-signposted technical squeeze that will last until the end of July. Daily premiums have been as high as $24, while the cash/threes backwardation neared $270 on Tuesday.
"No-one wants to pay these numbers, and the demand isn't there anyway in the summer. In theory, there are (physical) premiums, but in reality they are not," one trader said.
"Basically you do not have any buyers around...If you wanted to get a sale you could dip your premiums," another trader said.
In many cases, spot offers of as little as $5 over LME cash would be enough to transact business, the trader said.
However, on the spot market, there is very little incentive to buy anyway, with many European consumer works closing down for summer holidays.
"There are some enquiries with people looking to buy, but forward - you don't want to pay $20 or $30 over the (LME) settlement - the backwardation is the premium at the moment," said one.

On Wednesday, the LME cash/threes backwardation softened to around a still-high $185/200, while warehouse inventories soared 17,025 tonnes - an inevitable consequence of the squeeze attracting metal, traders said.
"This is a squeeze that will be overcome by the weight of incoming metal," another trader said.
The timing of the pressure on the market is also at odds with Northern Hemisphere summer fundamentals.
"A lot of rod-mills are closed in Europe, so there will be plenty of cathode available," he said.
Wednesday's inflow of metal will just be the start, as tonnages flood into Asia and the U.S. Some 50,000 tonnes is seen swelling stocks that currently stand at 160,325 tonnes.
Singapore will be the beneficiary of Chinese, Korean, and Taiwanese deliveries, while U.S. warehouses will see metal, both from Comex on arbitrage grounds, and U.S. producers, traders said.

Once the backwardations on the LME ease - this is expected from early-August - physical premiums are likely to revert to normal and hold steady during the rest of the second half of the year, some traders said.
"They should be good in the U.K., Italy, and Rotterdam...We are hearing that some rod producers in Germany are not closing because of good business on their books," one said..
